analysis.title: Marketcolour + RHM CEO Today / Prime Colour / Earnings Overview
key_insights: US equities closed Friday higher: SPX +31bps to 7376, NDX +135bps to 26989, RTY +89bps to 2754. Seven of 11 sectors fell, Tech rose +126bps, Staples fell -1.21% and Financials fell -0.68%.
NDX fell about 5% last week and has lost four weeks in a row. Semis are down about 28% over the last month.
The NFP print was hotter than expected at 165k actual vs 75k consensus, which lifted December hike odds to about 77%.
AI Semis (GSCBSMHX) rose +5.17% and Data Centers (GSTMTDAT) rose +4.99%. In Europe, EU Semis (GSSBSEMI) rose +1.6% while EU Defense (GSSBDEFE) fell -2.4% again.
11 of 20 European sectors have RSI above 70, the widest overbought reading since December 2023.
CTA positioning: long $23bn S&P (71st percentile) and short -$1bn NDX (35th percentile). GS sees big supply for the S&P in a flat tape under both scenarios, with the medium-term SPX pivot at 7547.
Prime book: US equities were modestly net sold on the week, with the largest single-stock net selling in 4 months partly offset by buying in Macro Products.

Info Tech was the most net sold sector globally and in the US by dollar value. Global Tech selling this week was about on par with the largest net-selling weeks on record (since 2016), and 4 of the top 5 such weeks have come in the past five months.

Hedge fund performance: global momentum fell 4.6 SD while crowded shorts squeezed +3.7 SD. Systematic L/S managers lost 1.5% on the week, their 4th straight weekly decline, and are still up 14.8% YTD.
Fundamental L/S managers lost 0.4% on the week and are up 8.7% YTD. Fundamental TMT managers fell almost 4% and are up only 1.3% YTD, against +25% at mid-year.

European earnings are beating expectations by 3.4% market-cap-weighted and 2.9% equal-weighted, slightly above historical norms. Misses are penalised more than beats are rewarded. Energy, Telecoms, Healthcare and Technology lead the beats.
Prysmian has the highest exposure to Texas among covered industrials, through the Encore Wire and Channell acquisitions and plans for 8 new medium voltage cable lines in the state.

Legrand has the largest datacenter business in GS coverage at 32% of sales and is more US-weighted than peers. It has derated significantly, and its non-datacenter business is among the most depressed in coverage because of heavy European residential exposure.
UniCredit net profit beat by 17%, with revenues 7% ahead, costs 2% below and loan loss provisions 10% below. NII was 3% above and fees 3% above.
Hannover Re missed on solvency by 14pp, though the absolute level is fine, and had a small P&C reinsurance revenue miss. GS calls it the default long in the space, and the stock is down about 1%.
GS rates Lancashire BUY with a GBP777 price target, 15% upside and a 12% dividend yield, citing earnings resilience from a broader underwriting portfolio.

market_movers.rationale: Lancashire has a broader underwriting portfolio and a less volatile earnings stream, so GS expects less contraction than in the previous soft cycle. Upside is 15% with a 12% dividend yield.
Hannover Re is described as the default long in the space despite a 14pp solvency miss and a small P&C revenue miss. The stock was down about 1%.
UniCredit beat on net profit by 17%, driven by revenues 7% ahead, costs 2% below and loan loss provisions 10% below.

sector_views.rationale: GS recommends shorting its Diversified Staples Basket (GSXUSTAP). Earnings and dividend yields are unattractive relative to fixed income, growth is thin, revisions are rolling over, and valuations sit in the 90th percentile relative to the last year.
Prime book data shows record-scale net selling in global Tech. GS reports the flows without giving a rating.
Prysmian has the most Texas exposure and Legrand the largest datacenter business in coverage. GS gives no rating on either.
